record.context_brief: Consecutive integers with prescribed gcd pattern.
record.original_question: Find the smallest integer k > 1 for which there exists an integer n such that gcd(n, n + k) = 1, but for every integer i with 1 <= i < k one has gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1.

evidence.quote: Find the smallest integer k > 1 and an integer n such that gcd(n, n + k) = 1 and gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1 for each i, 1 <= i < k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Determine the smallest integer k > 1 (if any) for which there exists a positive integer n satisfying both of the following conditions:

(a) gcd(n, n + k) = 1;
(b) for every integer i with 1 ≤ i < k, gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1.

In other words, among the k+1 consecutive integers n, n+1, …, n+k, the last one n+k is to be coprime to n while sharing a common factor greater than 1 with each of the intermediate terms n+1, n+2, …, n+k−1. Find the least such k together with an explicit n that witnesses it, or prove that no such pair (k, n) exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a Pillai-type problem on gcd-patterns among consecutive integers. Classical results of Pillai and Brauer establish that blocks of consecutive integers in which no term is coprime to all others first appear at length 17, but I could not locate a definitive published resolution of this exact variant (with the specific role played by the endpoint n+k). Status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Pillai's Problem on Consecutive Integers
status_evidence.snippet: Pillai and Brauer proved that for m ≥ 17 there exist blocks of m consecutive integers in which no element is coprime to all the others.
status_evidence.claim: Classical Pillai/Brauer results address related gcd-pattern questions on consecutive integers but do not directly settle the stated variant.

status_evidence.title: Sequences of Consecutive Integers (PEN A37 A9 O51)
status_evidence.snippet: Problems on consecutive integers and their pairwise gcd structure.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on the family of problems but does not resolve this particular question.
